title: Wheel and tyre specification change on a derivative variant
engineering_question: A chassis specification change is proposed for a derivative variant. What are the approval, energy and comfort consequences?
one_liner: Assess the compliance and certification consequences of this specification change.
initial_input: Engineering change ECR-006 introduces a larger wheel diameter and lower profile tyre specification on the top trim level, replacing the current specification.
expected_impacted_domains: Type approval for sound emission and tyre characteristics
Braking performance at revised rolling radius and mass
Tyre load capability at maximum axle load
expected_reasoning_paths: TR-025 rolling resistance failure propagates to REQ-001 certified range because DOC-004 allocates rolling resistance within the energy budget
TR-030 range pass was measured on the previous specification, so the certified range evidence does not cover the new variant
TR-028 pass-by noise not_run is a regulatory evidence gap on an approval-critical requirement
TR-029 axle load and load index verification not_run means REQ-121 tyre load capability is unverified while mass is also increasing from other proposed changes
This change interacts with ECR-001 and ECR-014, which both also affect mass, so the mass budget must be assessed across all three rather than individually
known_unknowns: Approval limit values are not held in the environment - only the regulation identifiers
The rolling radius change and its speedometer and range calibration effect is not quantified
Whether the derivative variant requires a separate approval extension is not recorded
data_classification: SIMULATED ENTERPRISE ARTEFACT - not OEM, customer or proprietary data
